districts.label: Financial District
districts.shortDescription: The Financial District is San Francisco’s densest concentration of traditional downtown office buildings. Large office towers, older high-rises and smaller professional buildings support finance, legal, corporate and business-service users that value a recognizable central address and proximity to other downtown firms. Compared with SoMa, the area feels more formal, vertically concentrated and oriented around established office blocks.
worthKnowing: Building age, floorplate and street activity vary sharply by block.
accessObservations: Embarcadero and Montgomery BART stations serve the downtown office core.

districts.label: SoMa
districts.oneLineDistinction: Large offices, tech and converted commercial buildings
districts.shortDescription: SoMa covers a broad mixed-use area where large modern offices sit near converted warehouses, creative workplaces, convention uses and smaller production-oriented buildings. Technology, creative and headquarters users often consider it for building variety and a less traditional downtown setting. The experience changes block by block, so Central SoMa, East SoMa and the waterfront edge should not be treated as interchangeable.
whatStandsOut: Mix of modern and adaptive-reuse buildings
worthKnowing: Confirm the exact SoMa subarea and building format before comparing options.
accessObservations: The Central Subway serves SoMa at 4th & Brannan and Yerba Buena/Moscone.

districts.label: Mission Bay
districts.oneLineDistinction: Newer research, medical and technical workplaces
districts.shortDescription: Mission Bay is a planned mixed-use district shaped by UCSF, medical facilities, research activity and newer commercial development. Life-science, technical and research users consider it for purpose-built or newer-generation workplaces and proximity to a larger institutional ecosystem. Its broad blocks and campus-like projects feel different from the older building fabric of SoMa or the traditional towers of the Financial District.
worthKnowing: Laboratory suitability, building systems and permitted use remain property-specific.
accessObservations: T Third light rail runs through Mission Bay along Third Street.

districts.label: Jackson Square
districts.oneLineDistinction: Historic, smaller-scale offices near the downtown core
districts.shortDescription: Jackson Square combines historic brick and masonry buildings with smaller offices, design businesses and client-facing professional firms. Users often consider it when they want character and a more intimate scale without leaving the downtown orbit. Its older, fine-grained building stock distinguishes it from Financial District towers and SoMa’s larger converted or newly developed spaces.
worthKnowing: Older buildings can differ materially in access, systems and interior configuration.

districts.label: South Beach / Embarcadero
districts.oneLineDistinction: Waterfront-edge offices south of the business core
districts.shortDescription: South Beach and the southern Embarcadero form a downtown-edge office setting between the Financial District, the waterfront and Mission Bay. Conventional office buildings mix with larger residential, event and mixed-use blocks. Businesses may consider it for a central-city location with a different street and waterfront context from the core Financial District, while still remaining connected to downtown commercial activity.
whatStandsOut: Mix of office and mixed-use blocks
worthKnowing: Event activity and building formats vary considerably around the ballpark and waterfront.
accessObservations: The area connects to downtown transit around Embarcadero and the Salesforce Transit Center.

districts.label: Union Square
districts.oneLineDistinction: Client-facing offices amid hotels and destination retail
districts.shortDescription: Union Square is best known as a retail and visitor district, but its upper floors and smaller commercial buildings also support professional, showroom and client-facing office users. It offers a busier hospitality and shopping context than a conventional office core. Businesses should distinguish the district’s public-facing setting from the quieter or more business-dense conditions found in the Financial District and Jackson Square.
worthKnowing: Street conditions and upper-floor access can differ substantially by building.
accessObservations: Union Square/Market Street station is on the Central Subway.

districts.label: Civic Center / Mid-Market
districts.oneLineDistinction: Government, nonprofit and institutional office concentration
districts.shortDescription: Civic Center and Mid-Market combine government offices, courts, cultural institutions, nonprofits and commercial buildings along and near Market Street. The area can suit organizations that work with public agencies or value an institutional setting, but the block-by-block experience is unusually varied. It is a different office proposition from the private-sector concentration of the Financial District or the creative and technology mix in SoMa.
worthKnowing: Visit the exact block and verify building access, condition and surrounding activity.

districts.label: Mission District
districts.oneLineDistinction: Neighborhood offices within active commercial streets
districts.shortDescription: The Mission is not a conventional office district. Its office options tend to sit in mixed-use buildings, converted commercial spaces and smaller workplaces near active neighborhood corridors. Creative firms, nonprofits and local service businesses may consider it for a neighborhood setting and proximity to food, retail and street life. It differs from SoMa through smaller scale and a more residential, corridor-based commercial fabric.
worthKnowing: Quiet office conditions, accessibility and building systems depend heavily on the property.

districts.label: Hayes Valley
districts.oneLineDistinction: Small offices in a design-led neighborhood setting
districts.shortDescription: Hayes Valley offers smaller office and studio settings within a compact neighborhood known for design, dining and independent retail. Creative, design, wellness and professional-service users may value the client-friendly street context more than large floorplates or a traditional business address. Its scale is more intimate than nearby Civic Center, while its commercial identity is more concentrated and customer-facing than a broad residential neighborhood.
worthKnowing: Large contiguous office requirements may be difficult to represent at district level.

districts.label: Presidio
districts.oneLineDistinction: Historic campus workplaces inside a national park
districts.shortDescription: The Presidio offers a specialized office setting in reused military buildings within a federally managed national park. Technology, finance, education, nonprofit and creative organizations occupy a mix of multi-tenant and stand-alone buildings. The low-density campus character is unlike downtown towers or neighborhood storefront offices, making it a meaningful niche option rather than a substitute for every conventional San Francisco office search.
worthKnowing: Leasing rules, transportation, parking and building conditions require Presidio-specific review.
